title: Reduce size of wallpapers by using compressed AVIF as the file format
line: The default and bundled wallpapers now ship as AVIF, so they take about 15 MB on disk instead of 320 MB and load faster.
explanation: The Breeze Next wallpaper (39 MB) and the wallpapers in plasma-workspace-wallpapers (280 MB) were shipped as PNG, which makes packages large and the images slow to decode at login, on the lock screen and in the wallpaper picker. A few places also hardcoded the Next PNG file names (SDDM's default background, Welcome Center's mock desktops, plasma-setup's landing page). Every wallpaper PNG is now AVIF (quality 90, 4:4:4, encoded with libaom through libheif), so Next is under 1 MB and the extra wallpapers 14 MB, with no visible difference; both wallpaper repos list kimageformats built with libavif as a runtime dependency, and the hardcoded paths point to the AVIF files.

commits.message:
wallpapers: ship Next as AVIF instead of PNG

The Next images were 39 MB of PNGs that are slow to decode at login
and on the lock screen. Ship them as AVIF (under 1 MB in total) and
declare kimageformats with libavif as a runtime dependency.

BUG: 474862

Ship wallpapers as AVIF instead of PNG

The PNG wallpapers took up 280 MB and were slow to decode. Convert them
to AVIF at quality 90, which brings them to 14 MB with no visible loss,
and declare kimageformats with libavif as a runtime dependency.

BUG: 474862

sddm-theme: use the AVIF version of the Next wallpaper

Breeze now ships the Next wallpaper as AVIF instead of PNG, so the
default SDDM background pointed to a file that no longer exists. Point
it to the AVIF image instead.

BUG: 474862

Use the AVIF version of the Next wallpaper in mock desktops

Breeze now ships the Next wallpaper as AVIF instead of PNG, so the
mock desktops pointed to a file that no longer exists and showed no
wallpaper. Point them to the AVIF image instead.

BUG: 474862

Use the AVIF version of the Next wallpaper on the landing page

Breeze now ships the Next wallpaper as AVIF instead of PNG, so the
landing page looked for files that no longer exist and showed no
background. Look for the AVIF images instead.

BUG: 474862
